reason: E1 shows that a high-entropy oxide stabilizes Pt nanoparticles against sintering and water, but it does not demonstrate single-atom Pt or atomic layer deposition. E2 shows that Pd doping on a high-entropy oxide dramatically lowers CO oxidation onset temperature via a Mars–van Krevelen mechanism, but it uses Pd, not Pt, and does not address single-atom dispersion or NO/H2O poisoning resistance. The key premises about single-atom Pt creation, synergistic electronic modification, and combined poisoning resistance are not directly supported by the cited evidence.
premises: Single-atom Pt sites can be created on a high-entropy substrate via atomic layer deposition.
A high-entropy substrate stabilizes supported Pt against sintering under hydrothermal aging.
Doping a high-entropy oxide with a platinum-group metal dramatically lowers CO oxidation onset temperature.
The Mars–van Krevelen mechanism operates on metal-doped reducible high-entropy oxides for CO oxidation.
